correctness.rationale: At the boundary i,i+1 the change in excedance count is [π_{i+1}=i+1]−[π_i=i+1]. Since entries are distinct, legality excludes that value in both slots, so no moved value changes excedance status. For any top set T⊆{2,…,n}, the canonical word lists T increasingly and its complement increasingly. The j-th top is ≥j+1 and the j-th complement value is ≤|T|+j, so the canonical word realizes T. Sorting in this order is legal: an adjacent inverted pair within T has both entries >i+1, an inverted pair in the complement has both <i+1, and a cross-block inversion moves each entry away from its threshold. This proves connectivity and the two-sort bound n(n−1). For T={2,…,k+1}, every boundary of the canonical word contains its forbidden value; hence that word is isolated and its fiber is a singleton. Otherwise the first top t_j>j+1 can be swapped with the next top or with 1 if j=k, so its connected fiber is nontrivial. For the edge count, the two forbidden events at each boundary are disjoint. Deleting a fixed point removes its row and column with all other strict excedance comparisons unchanged. Deleting π_i=i+1 removes row i and column i+1; the remaining rows before i and after i keep the same comparison signs, including at surviving column i and row i+1. Thus the counts of blocked incidences are A(n−1,k) and A(n−1,k−1) per boundary; subtraction and division by two gives the result. This also covers k=0, k=n−1 and n=2 under the stated convention. The frozen scripts were inspected but not executed. A separate bounded breadth-first search using the strict top-set test found distance 8 and 31 reachable vertices in the illustrative n=5 fiber {4,5}; the unrestricted relative permutation has 6 inversions.
residual_risks: The supplied Python tests finite dimensions and the C++ DSU checks finite component and edge incidences, not the all-n Eulerian formula independently. Expected console lines in the frozen verification are not fresh run logs.

evidence: 79c08e75f702 classifies components by strict left/right signs for the forbidden fixed-point labels, with 2^|F∩{2,…,n−1}| components. Its proof sorts the left, unrestricted, and right blocks. The two derangement graphs have restricted vertices, and the cyclic one adds the wraparound move. Pierrot–Rossin–West replace patterns in consecutive positions based on relative order.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The fixed-point theorem forbids equality for every constrained label; here equality is allowed and belongs to the nonexcedance side. Even with all fixed points forbidden, legality differs: a derangement cannot move π_{i+1}=i into position i, whereas the fixed-excedance rule can do so if neither entry equals i+1. The same sorting argument transfers after checking the changed constraints, but the stated graph theorems are not equivalent. The relative-order pattern rule is also not the absolute label threshold i+1.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Once the moves and their preserved fibers are proved, the number of components follows from realizability and the familiar binomial count. But realizing or counting a fiber does not establish its legal connectivity, and the strict-side result does not enumerate blocked boundary incidences in this graph. The separate local threshold and deletion identities establish those conclusions; no checked prior statement supplies them mechanically.

evidence: The inverse gives a deficiency-position set {v:π⁻¹(v)<v}; reflecting both indices and values converts it to a strict excedance-position set. Thus classical position-set enumeration can enumerate the fibers as sets. The tableau paper defines the weak-excedance top π(i) at an index with π(i)≥i.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The inverse turns an original adjacent-position swap into a swap of adjacent labels, not generally positions. Counting a fiber via that bijection does not prove it is connected in the original graph. Weak-excedance top statistics also include fixed points, unlike this invariant.

originality.rationale: The distinct claim is the top-value component classification for strict fixed-excedance strata of all permutations under consecutive-position swaps, including its isolates and edge formula. Value-side excedance statistics, fiber enumeration under inverse/reflection, and the closely related side-signature bubble-sort method are not claimed as new. The strongest same-day forbidden-fixed-point record uses the same sorting idea but a different vertex constraint and threshold; its theorem does not give this move rule, classification, or edge statistic.
residual_risks: The exact definition in Baril–Mansour–Petrossian could not be compared from primary text. The inspected results establish method and statistic overlaps, not historical priority; an unindexed equivalent graph theorem is not excluded.

value.rationale: A classical statistic defines a natural subgraph of the permutahedron. The theorem gives complete reachability information in all strata via a simple conserved set, an explicit path construction, and exact isolation and edge counts. These answer structural questions not resolved by the classical Eulerian enumeration of vertices alone.
residual_risks: The diameter bound is not an exact general intra-fiber metric or a formula for component sizes.
